assessment: This fundamental work presents two clinically relevant BMP4 mutations that contribute to vertebrate development. The compelling evidence, both from wet lab and AI generated predictions, supports that the site-specific cleavage at the BMP4 pro-domain precisely regulates its function and provides mechanistic insight how homodimers and heterodimers behave differently. The work will be of broad interest to researchers working on growth factor signaling mechanisms and vertebrate development.
